cloud_sdks.basis: AWS exposes Python access through Boto3, the official AWS SDK maintained by Amazon; Microsoft Azure exposes its service plane through the Azure SDK for Python, a suite of per-service packages published under the azure- namespace on PyPI.

container_orchestration.basis: docker-py and the official kubernetes Python client are the standard tooling; Kubernetes cluster provisioning, Helm chart templating, and operator development increasingly rely on Python tooling (e.g., the kubernetes Python client, Kopf framework for operators).

iac_configuration_management.basis: Ansible is an open source, command-line IT automation software application written in Python, making it the reference implementation language for one of the dominant configuration-management/IaC tools.

messaging_streaming.basis: kafka-python/confluent-kafka-python and pika (RabbitMQ) are the widely used default client libraries.

ml_ai_bindings.basis: The scientific Python stack — NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch — maps directly onto managed ML services, and AWS SageMaker's Python SDK (sagemaker package) wraps training jobs, model endpoints, and pipeline steps in Python objects.

nosql_stores.basis: pymongo (MongoDB), redis-py (Redis) and the cassandra-driver are the de-facto default client libraries used across the ecosystem.

observability.basis: OpenTelemetry Python ships an official API and SDK, available on PyPI, and can be installed via pip: pip install opentelemetry-api pip install opentelemetry-sdk, with the Traces and Metrics signals marked Stable.

relational_db_drivers.basis: psycopg/psycopg2 (PostgreSQL), mysqlclient/PyMySQL (MySQL) and the standard-library sqlite3 module are the long-standing de-facto default drivers used across the ecosystem.

rpc_schema_protocols.basis: Python has excellent gRPC support through the grpcio library, and Azure Container Apps can host gRPC services with proper HTTP/2 support.

web_frameworks.basis: Django, Flask and FastAPI are mainstream, actively maintained web frameworks each with large plugin ecosystems.

checklist_10_domains_10pts_each: Major public cloud provider SDKs (AWS, Azure, GCP)
NoSQL / distributed data stores (MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra)
Mainstream web frameworks with broad third-party ecosystems
rubric_frozen_for_all_10_languages.conversion: sum of the 10 per-domain scores = 0-100 normalized score
rubric_frozen_for_all_10_languages.definition: Breadth and reliability of actively-maintained, production-ready working integrations with external systems and platforms (not the language's FFI/interop design, which is scored under Language Quality).

per_domain_scale.10: an official or de-facto-standard, actively maintained library exists and is the community default
per_domain_scale.4: only partial/experimental or unmaintained integrations exist
per_domain_scale.7: a mature, widely used third-party library exists but is not an unambiguous single default

android.basis: The initial goal is for Android to achieve Tier 3 support in Python 3.13, per PEP 738 (Adding Android as a supported platform).

bsd_other_unix.basis: PEP 11 lists platforms not officially supported by the PSF; these can still be supported by external ports, and FreeBSD/other BSDs run CPython via such community ports rather than an official PSF tier.

ios.basis: Official supported tier-3 systems include 64-bit ARM Windows, 64-bit iOS, Raspberry Pi OS (Linux for armv7 with hard float), Linux for 64-bit PowerPC in little-endian mode, and Linux for s390x.

linux_arm64.basis: Official tier-2 support exists for Linux for 64-bit ARM, wasm32 (Web Assembly) with WASI runtime support, and Linux for 64-bit Intel using a clang toolchain.

linux_x86_64.basis: Officially supported tier-1 platforms are Linux for 64-bit Intel using a GCC toolchain, macOS for 64-bit Intel and ARM, and Microsoft Windows for 32- and 64-bit Intel.

other_secondary_arch.basis: Tier-3 also covers Linux 64-bit PowerPC (little-endian) and s390x, per the same tier-3 listing cited above.

python_cpython_scoring.source: PEP 11 (CPython platform support) and companion PEPs 730/738/816, cross-checked against Wikipedia's CPython summary, snapshot 2026-09-22

webassembly_wasi.basis: WASI was a tier 3 platform for Python 3.11 and 3.12, and became a tier 2 platform starting with Python 3.13.

windows_x86_64.basis: tier-1, see linux_x86_64 citation covering Windows 32/64-bit Intel

checklist_10_platforms_10pts_each: Other/secondary CPU architecture (e.g. s390x, POWER, RISC-V)
rubric_frozen_for_all_10_languages.conversion: sum of the 10 per-platform scores = 0-100 normalized score
rubric_frozen_for_all_10_languages.definition: Breadth of platforms on which the language's primary/reference implementation has official, currently-maintained implemented support (not merely language-level portability, which is scored under Language Quality).

per_platform_scale.10: official tier-1 / first-class, fully supported and tested by the core maintainers
per_platform_scale.3: no official support, but a well-established third-party port/toolchain exists
per_platform_scale.6: official tier-3 / experimental but merged and shipped by the core project
per_platform_scale.8: official tier-2 (supported and tested, but with narrower guarantees than tier-1)

rubric_frozen_for_all_10_languages.source_rule: Use the language's own official platform-support policy document/PEP/RFC where one exists; snapshot date 2026-09-22.

notes.limitations: Per-platform/per-domain tier scales are an objective, frozen proxy applied identically across languages by construction; they are not raw popularity counts and are not used as a standalone whole-evaluation proxy.
notes.scope: This shard evaluates only the Python column for metric.implemented_platform_coverage and metric.external_integration_coverage under the ecosystem evaluation, per the assigned-language restriction in the task packet.
